scenario.title: Late shipments
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

M-HANDOVER-LATE-RATE.name: Share of orders recorded late at the handover stage

M-ORDERS-RELEASED-AFTER-PICKUP.name: Count of orders released after carrier pickup had occurred

F-01.statement: 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are late at the handover stage per order-db.late_orders_by_stage.

F-02.statement: pickup-log recorded a median 2-hour pickup delay across 60 pickups (pickup_delays method).

F-03.statement: wms-jobs RELEASE-BATCH job had 21 failed runs out of 30, with 290 orders released after the carrier pickup had already occurred.

F-04.statement: Carrier contract §3 states that pickup schedule changes proceed only after SH-CAR confirms, matching the K-SCHED human-approval constraint.

F-05.statement: pickup-log pickup_by_slot recorded an identical 2.0h delay across all 6 sampled slots (S-0 to S-5).

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

CL-02.statement: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

H-INFO-GAP.statement: Parcels are not actually delayed beyond normal variance; the problem is customers lack visibility into existing delay reasons, so an explanatory chatbot resolves the complaint.

H-WAREHOUSE-DELAY.statement: Shipments are genuinely late because warehouse picking/packing jobs in ORG-1 routinely run behind schedule before handoff to the carrier.

H-HANDOFF-DEFECT.statement: Lateness stems from unreliable or invalid handoffs between Shop and Carrier (H-PICK), e.g. parcels not properly registered or confirmed for pickup.

H-CARRIER-SCHEDULE-MISMATCH.statement: Lateness is caused by delays in confirming carrier pickup schedule changes, since K-SCHED requires carrier human approval before any push_pickup_schedule action takes effect.

H-INACCURATE-ETA.statement: Shipments are not operationally late, but promised delivery dates recorded in DA-ORD are set too optimistically, making normal timelines appear late to customers.

H-PICKUP-LOG-CONSTANT-ARTIFACT.statement: The identical 2.0h delay_h value across all 6 pickup_by_slot records may reflect a fixed/default instrumentation value rather than independently measured per-slot delays, which would undermine using this data to assess H-PICK semantic validity.

interpretation_history.interpretation: order-db shows 300 of 1000 orders (30%) recorded late specifically at the "handover" stage, meaning lateness is detectable at the point parcels transition from warehouse (ORG-1) to carrier (ORG-CAR), not only at final delivery. This localizes the lateness signal to the warehouse/handoff boundary, bearing on warehouse-delay and handoff-defect hypotheses while weakening explanations resting on ETA optimism or pure customer information gaps.

pickup-log reports a median 2-hour delay across 60 carrier pickups, giving a concrete delay magnitude at the Shop→Carrier handoff point (H-PICK). This confirms a real, measurable operational delay exists at pickup, but does not by itself distinguish whether the cause is carrier schedule-confirmation friction (K-SCHED) or handoff registration/validity defects.

E-03.content: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-LOG (logistics lead, non-authoritative interview) claims parcels are late because the carrier picks up two hours late. This is an unverified causal claim pointing to the carrier pickup stage, distinct from the requester's (CL-01) "customer information gap" framing, and not itself backed by tool evidence.

wms-jobs reports 21 of 30 RELEASE-BATCH runs failed and 290 orders were released only after the carrier had already picked up, showing a concrete warehouse-side (ORG-1) mechanism — batch release job failures — that causes orders to miss the pickup window, independent of when the carrier actually arrives.

E-05.content: Carrier contract §3: pickup schedule changes run after SH-CAR confirms.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The carrier contract (E-05) confirms that any push_pickup_schedule change requires SH-CAR's confirmation, procedurally substantiating the K-SCHED human-approval constraint; it is an authorization/procedure fact, not new evidence about the cause of lateness.

pickup-log's slot-level breakdown shows an identical 2.0-hour delay across all 6 sampled pickup slots (S-0 through S-5), confirming the E-02 median of 2h is not slot-dependent. The complete absence of variance across slots suggests a systematic, constant offset rather than slot-specific carrier scheduling friction or variable handoff registration irregularities.

U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY.question: Would fixing RELEASE-BATCH job failures reduce the median 2-hour pickup delay (E-02), or is some of that delay independent of warehouse release timing?
U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY.decision_impact: Determines whether a warehouse-only fix suffices or whether carrier-side coordination (push_pickup_schedule) is also needed to close the gap.
U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY.resolution_path: Correlate per-order release timestamps with pickup timestamps across order-db, wms-jobs and pickup-log once remediation is underway.
U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY.safe_placeholder: Proceed with warehouse RELEASE-BATCH diagnosis as the primary track; treat carrier pickup-schedule adjustment as an optional parallel mitigation, not a precondition.

U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.question: What causes the RELEASE-BATCH job failures themselves (e.g. the ACCESS_PENDING hold recorded in recent operational events)?
U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation is a wms-jobs access/configuration fix or a deeper warehouse process redesign.
U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Investigate the wms-jobs NOT_TRANSIENT hold with the warehouse systems admin (SH-WMS) once access is restored.
U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Track release_batch_failure_rate as the monitored metric without assuming a specific root cause for the job failures yet.

U-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-VALIDITY.question: Is the Shop→Carrier handoff (H-PICK) actually defective in registration/confirmation, or is its semantic_validity simply unmeasured (currently UNKNOWN)?
U-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Bears on whether handoff-registration fixes (H-HANDOFF-DEFECT) are needed alongside the warehouse batch-job fix.
U-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Audit a sample of H-PICK handoff records for registration/confirmation status.
U-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Continue monitoring handover_late_rate without assuming the handoff registration mechanism itself is broken.

A-RELEASE-CAUSES-LATE.statement: The 290 orders released after pickup (E-04) are largely the same population driving the 300/1000 handover-late orders (E-01), rather than a disjoint subset.

A-PICKUP-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 60 sampled pickups in pickup-log (E-02) are representative of overall carrier pickup timing despite DA-PICK completeness being UNKNOWN.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late (CL-01, SH-CX).
symptoms: 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are recorded late specifically at the handover stage (E-01).
Median carrier pickup delay of 2 hours across 60 sampled pickups (E-02).
Customers complain their parcels are late, prompting the chatbot request (CL-01).
problem_definition.root_problem: 30% of orders (300/1000) are recorded late at the warehouse-to-carrier handover stage (E-01); this is caused by failures in the warehouse's RELEASE-BATCH job (21 of 30 runs failed), which left 290 orders released from the warehouse only after the carrier had already completed pickup (E-04), i.e. warehouse release-process failures, not carrier tardiness or a customer information gap, drive the lateness.

actions.decision_impact_rationale: Determines whether the next step is a warehouse-process fix, handoff fix, or no operational fix at all (info-gap chatbot).
actions.why_now: DA-ORD completeness is UNKNOWN and CL-01's root-cause claim is UNVERIFIED; this is the foundational data query before any downstream analysis.

proposal.summary: The original request (CL-01, from SH-CX) was to build a chatbot explaining parcel lateness, but evidence redefined the actual problem as warehouse-side release failures: 30% of orders are late at the handover stage (E-01), traced to RELEASE-BATCH job failures (21/30 runs, 290 orders released after carrier pickup; E-04), not carrier tardiness or customer information gaps (both corresponding hypotheses were REJECTED). The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns as open verification obligations. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with nothing held back, but the released scope is narrow: only monitoring the handover late-rate (DA-ORD) and verifying H-PICK handoff semantic validity. The warehouse diagnosis action (DA-WMS) and the carrier-scheduling action (push_pickup_schedule:H-PICK) remain outside scope because the verification obligations blocking them are still open, and the root-cause access/config fix on wms-jobs is deemed not feasible within contest time. Several open unknowns, a non-critical verification obligation about slot-delay data quality, and unknown data completeness for the warehouse log are documented as explicit limitations of this release.
key_points: The customer-facing request (CL-01, SH-CX) was to build a chatbot explaining parcel lateness, but investigation reframed the problem: 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are late specifically at the warehouse-to-carrier handover stage (E-01).

Root cause was traced to warehouse-side RELEASE-BATCH job failures: 21 of 30 runs failed, and 290 orders were released only after the carrier had already picked up (E-04), rather than carrier tardiness (H-CARRIER-SCHEDULE-MISMATCH, REJECTED) or a customer information gap (H-INFO-GAP, REJECTED).
A median 2-hour carrier pickup delay was also measured (E-02), identical across all 6 sampled slots (E-06), supporting H-WAREHOUSE-DELAY (CONFIRMED) and H-HANDOFF-DEFECT (SUPPORTED).

The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY, U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE) as open verification obligations rather than blocking everything.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items held back; released scope is limited to monitor_handover_late_rate:DA-ORD and verify_handoff_semantic_validity:H-PICK (per solution_design SD-1).

diagnose_release_batch_failures:DA-WMS and the carrier-scheduling action push_pickup_schedule:H-PICK were kept out of release scope because the VOBs blocking them (VOB-U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY, VOB-U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE) remain OPEN.

Fixing the warehouse RELEASE-BATCH ACCESS_PENDING access/config/ownership issue (owned by ORG-1/SH-WMS) was identified as the action that would remove the root cause, but it was judged not feasible in contest time and so is not part of this release.
limitations_explained: Two HIGH-impact unknowns remain unresolved and sit outside release scope: whether fixing RELEASE-BATCH would actually reduce the 2-hour pickup delay (U-FIX-REDUCES-PICKUP-DELAY), and what causes the RELEASE-BATCH job failures themselves, e.g. the ACCESS_PENDING hold (U-JOB-FAILURE-ROOT-CAUSE).

VOB-R-3 (non-critical, intersecting release scope) is open: it is unverified whether the identical 2.0h delay across all 6 pickup slots (E-06) is a genuine per-slot measurement or an instrumentation artifact, which affects whether that data truly establishes H-PICK's registration/confirmation validity.
Completeness of DA-ORD and DA-PICK is COMPLETE, but DA-WMS completeness is UNKNOWN, which limits confidence in any monitoring or verification results drawn from the warehouse job log.
H-PICK semantic_validity is UNKNOWN and will only be assessed by the scoped verify_handoff_semantic_validity check now included in the release; it is not yet confirmed as defective or sound.

The underlying ACCESS_PENDING access/config/ownership condition behind RELEASE-BATCH failures (owned by ORG-1/SH-WMS) has not been fixed in this release; it must be resolved separately and not through carrier scheduling.
Even after a warehouse-side fix, carrier-side pickup timing dynamics unrelated to warehouse release failures may still cause some delay, per the stated known limitation.

push_pickup_schedule requires SH-CAR's human approval per K-SCHED/E-05, but this action and the DA-WMS diagnosis work item are excluded from this release because their blocking VOBs are still open, not because they were evaluated and cleared.
